title: Helium-3 extraction economics
bottleneck: Lunar regolith holds helium-3 at parts-per-billion levels from solar-wind implantation; recovering kilograms requires heating millions of tons of regolith to about 700 C to release trapped gases, then separating He-3 from far more abundant He-4. The energy cost is staggering, the machinery would be the largest industrial operation ever attempted off Earth, and there is no fusion reactor to buy the product. It is a supply chain for a demand that does not exist, each side waiting for the other.
why_it_blocks: Helium-3 is routinely cited as the Moon's killer resource; if extraction is uneconomic, the lunar mining business case rests on water alone.
current_state: No extraction has ever been attempted; estimates remain paper studies. All serious ISRU planning targets water and oxygen.
